articles.title: NASCAR legend Tony Stewart's return to the Truck Series ends early with big crash at Talladega
articles.excerpt:
Ross Chastain questions if Stephen A. Smith could even recognize a NASCAR driver in a recent interview with OutKick.

For the second race this season, NASCAR great Tony Stewart hopped into a Craftsman...
articles.body_text:
Ross Chastain questions if Stephen A. Smith could even recognize a NASCAR driver in a recent interview with OutKick.

For the second race this season, NASCAR great Tony Stewart hopped into a Craftsman Truck Series truck, but fans unfortunately didn’t get much time to see Smoke doing his thing at Talladega Superspeedway.

Back in February, Stewart made his return to NASCAR competition when he drove the No. 25 Ram 1500 for Kaulig Racing.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

That ended with a crash 39 laps into the race, so Stewart was surely hoping — and fans certainly were too — that he would make it the full race distance.

NASCAR FANS PACK INTO TALLADEGA SUPERSPEEDWAY AHEAD OF SUNDAY'S JACK LINKS 500 RACE

NASCAR great Tony Stewart made his second Craftsman Truck Series start of the season on Saturday at Talladega. (Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Unfortunately, his time on track was even shorter.

The race got off to a good start for Stewart. He qualified 29th, but was able to gain 11 positions in the first 15 laps.

But on lap 17, Stewart Friesen lost control of his No. 52 Toyota Tundra on the backstretch, which caused a big, nine-car wreck.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That was it for Stewart, which is a real shame for a few reasons. First of all, it sure seems like that truck of his had some potential, given how many positions he picked up early. Secondly, fans didn't get to see as much of the NASCAR Hall of Famer back on track.

Hey, that is the reality of superspeedway racing. You need a good helping of luck to go along with that quick truck.

Tony Stewart climbs into his race truck during qualifying for the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series Playoffs Loves's RV Stop 225 at Talladega Superspeedway. (Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

"Yeah, it’s just a racing deal," Stewart said, per the Associated Press. "That’s part of it. Stewart (Friesen) couldn’t go anywhere. He had an issue, and he’s stuck in the middle. So he was doing the best he could to hang onto it, and just everybody around him got caught up in it."

Well, maybe we'll get to see Stewart back in the Truck Series at some point next season. There aren't any concrete plans, but he's certainly due for some good luck.

The race win ended up going to Spire Motorsports' Sammy Smith, who managed to take the checkered flag in overtime. It was Smith's first career Truck Series win and came the same day that it was announced that he will compete full-time for Tricon Garage next season.

articles.title: McMahon plans to 'fire' herself out of a job, striving to show Congress that the Dept of Ed is not needed
articles.excerpt:
Linda McMahon asks Congress to let her prove the Department of Education can be dismantled without disrupting federal student loans or K-12 funding.

U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon doubled dow...
articles.body_text:
Linda McMahon asks Congress to let her prove the Department of Education can be dismantled without disrupting federal student loans or K-12 funding.

U.S. Education Secretary Linda McMahon doubled down on closing the Department of Education (ED) as planned to demonstrate to Congress that the federal agency she leads is no longer necessary.

"Signing these interagency agreements means, in fact, that the Department of Education is contracting with these agencies to perform the functions that they've been given," McMahon told Fox News Digital.

"The first big block of work was transferred over to the Department of Labor."

Throughout his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump promised to eliminate the ED, later signing an executive order directing his administration to begin dismantling the agency.

MCMAHON EMBARKS ON FOUR-STATE TOUR TO PUT LOCAL LEADERS AND PARENTS 'BACK INTO THE DRIVER’S SEAT' OF EDUCATION

Education Secretary Linda McMahon outside the White House in Washington, D.C., July 15, 2025. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

As part of that effort, the Department of Labor (DOL) is taking on a major role in the day-to-day administration of adult education, family literacy and career and technical education (CTE) programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) and the Perkins Act.

While Labor manages operational duties, the Department of Education retains statutory responsibilities and oversight while shifting services to states and grant recipients.

"It started first with CTE — Career and Technical Education — then K–12 and finally higher education as well," McMahon said.

McMahon explained that she wants to show lawmakers that federal support for students won't falter without a standalone Cabinet department.

"I've asked Congress with this proof of concept in these interagency agreements: 'Let me prove to you that it works,'" she said.

"Ultimately, Congress has to vote if we do close the Department of Education, and if I, in fact, am able to fire myself. Hopefully, they will vote [for it], because I believe the outcome will be better for students, and that is the goal. That is certainly the president's goal."

TRUMP ADMIN URGES RETURNING EDUCATION TO STATES, CITING $3 TRILLION OF TAXES SPENT AND POOR PROFICIENCY SCORES

A Department of Education sign is displayed outside its federal student aid office May 18, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

The agency took another major step by partnering with the Department of the Treasury, which agreed to take over key operations related to federal student loans and collections on defaulted debt.

The student loan partnership with Treasury and the workforce initiative with DOL are part of a broader series of interagency agreements. According to Department of Education officials, the goal is to demonstrate a "proof of concept" to Congress that essential federal education functions and funding flows can be successfully reallocated across executive branch agencies without disruption.

"I call it my proof of concept to show Congress that it works, that the money still gets to schools and to students where they need it," McMahon told Fox News Digital.

"Some of the programs in the Department of Education were being duplicated in other agencies or handled better elsewhere," McMahon added. "So, let's be efficient. Let's make sure the money gets where it needs to go, let's measure that by student outcomes and let's hold teachers and administrators accountable for what they're doing."

Andrew Gillen, a higher education policy research fellow at the Cato Institute, told Fox News Digital that shifting major core duties like student loans and formula grants marks a substantial change from previous interagency agreements, which historically focused on minor administrative support.

McMahon previously argued during the government shutdown that the ED acts primarily as a pass-through entity for federal money, contending that its day-to-day functions are nonessential.

"Congress appropriates the funds. The funds come through the Department of Education, and some of that funding still goes to other agencies to get to students and schools," McMahon told Fox News Digital.

"Primarily, the money was passed through the Department of Education to then get to the states and local authorities for education."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TARGETS HEAD START BUREAUCRACY IN MOVE ADVOCATES SAY PUTS PARENTS IN THE DRIVER'S SEAT

President Donald Trump holds up an executive order to start dismantling the Department of Education after signing it in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., March 20, 2025.  (Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty Images)

ED announced earlier this year that the agency moved out of the Lyndon B. Johnson Department of Education building so the Department of Energy could move in by August. The move is what the officials call "a prudent step to save hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars and further reduce the federal education bureaucracy."

The Trump administration is also seeking to reduce the department's footprint by returning more power to the states.

The ED launched a new process allowing states to seek greater flexibility in using federal education funds and reducing administrative burdens. Iowa became the first state to participate in the effort.

The Department of Education sent states a letter in July 2025 encouraging them to apply for the waiver, which would give state education officials more discretion over federal dollars and reduce compliance costs.

Joshua Q. Nelson is a reporter for Fox News Digital.

Joshua focuses on cultural trends, education, and public policy. He extensively covered reparations developments across the U.S., the Department of Education, and immigration issues.

Joining Fox News Digital in 2019, he previously graduated from Syracuse University's Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs and received the University of Pennsylvania's Wharton Public Policy Certificate.

Story tips can be sent to joshua.nelson@fox.com and Joshua can be followed on Instagram, Twitter and LinkedIn.

articles.title: Tyler Robinson hearing ends without trial date set, prompting fiery plea from Erika Kirk's lawyer
articles.excerpt: Former federal prosecutor Fred Tecce told Fox News Digital that Tyler Robinson’s defense is pushing for a 2029 trial in the Charlie Kirk assassination case as a delay tactic, noting Utah law gives vic...
articles.body_text:
Former federal prosecutor Fred Tecce told Fox News Digital that Tyler Robinson’s defense is pushing for a 2029 trial in the Charlie Kirk assassination case as a delay tactic, noting Utah law gives victims a right to a speedy trial.

PROVO, Utah — Tyler Robinson, the 23-year-old Utah man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk at a Turning Point USA event last year, still doesn't have a trial date after a Utah judge listened to oral arguments from both sides — and a lawyer for Kirk's widow — about how much time they think they'll need and when they'd like to start.

Robinson, wearing a light gray suit, uncuffed and unshackled, did not address the court. He spoke quietly with attorneys Richard Novak, Kathy Nester and Staci Visser during breaks, at one point handing Visser a note.

Judge Tony Graf Jr. said he had planned to set a trial date at the end of the hearing but needed more time after questioning both sides about their expected timelines and commitments in previously scheduled trials on other cases.

Jeffrey Neiman, an attorney for Kirk's widow, Erika, pleaded with the court to speed things up. Robinson did not enter a plea until last month, nearly a year after being charged.

LAWYERS FOR CHARLIE KIRK'S ACCUSED ASSASSIN TYLER ROBINSON WANT CAMERAS BANNED AFTER REPORT ON TAXPAYER BURDEN

Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family.

Jeffrey Adam Nieman, attorney for Erika Kirk, attends a pretrial hearing for Tyler James Robinson, 23, who is charged with aggravated murder and six other counts in the Sept. 10, 2025, fatal shooting of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University, in 4th District Court on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Provo, Utah. (Erin Hooley, Deseret News via Pool)

"Every day of delay adds to uncertainty, invites speculation, and that erodes confidence in this system," Neiman said at one point.

The roughly three-hour hearing saw several interruptions due to technical difficulty with WebEx, with Robinson defense attorney Michael Burt and an attorney for Kirk's parents, Robert and Kathy, attending remotely.

Utah County prosecutors had floated Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027.

Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk, is seen in court in his first in-person court appearance on Dec. 11, 2025. (Pool/KSL-TV)

TYLER ROBINSON TO FACE TRIAL IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION AS JUDGE KEEPS DEATH PENALTY ON TABLE

Visser said that pretrial litigation "builds upon itself," and given that there are over 31,000 pieces of discovery and "8 million" artifacts of digital evidence, they will need time to file motions to compel, file subpoenas, etc.

"Discovery review is foundational," she said. "It impacts everything else."

As a result, she said, the state’s proposed January 2028 trial is "not practical."

Defense attorney Staci Visser attends a pretrial hearing for Tyler James Robinson, 23, who is charged with aggravated murder and six other counts in the Sept. 10, 2025, fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University, in 4th District Court, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Provo, Utah.

The defense had asked for a "soft target" date in the third quarter of 2029, citing large amounts of discovery and other trial preparations — as well as trial commitments in other cases. Among those, one directly conflicted with the prosecution's desired start date, a federal racketeering case defense attorney Novak has scheduled for Jan. 10, 2028.

Both sides agreed that setting a trial that would run through the holidays could put potential jurors and witnesses in a bind.

ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR

"Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family," Neiman said.

Defense attorney Richard Novak attends a pretrial hearing for Tyler James Robinson, 23, who is charged with aggravated murder and six other counts in the Sept. 10, 2025, fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University, in 4th District Court, Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Provo, Utah.

Neiman noted that only about 5% of federal cases actually make it to trial and said the Kirk family would be happy to write to the federal judge and ask for the January trial to be rescheduled to clear up Robinson's defense attorney.

Under Utah's state constitution, victims and their representatives have a right to a speedy resolution to their case. Erika Kirk is the court's designated victim's representative.

Novak told the court that trial's start date had been "set in stone" and argued against rushing things along in the case against Robinson.

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

"The reality is rushing to trial does not lead to closure, it does not lead to finality, it leads to mistakes," he said.

UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE

Graf expressed concern that if he does not set a date soon, additional conflicts could arise.

Erika Kirk departs court in Provo, Utah, Monday, July 6, 2026. The widow of Charlie Kirk was attending the first day of preliminary hearings against Tyler Robinson. (Alec Thornock for Fox News Digital)

Neiman, who is primarily a criminal defense attorney, has repeatedly asked the court to speed things up.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"Time is the defense’s best ally," he said. "It’s their best friend."

He also noted that regardless of when the trial takes place, Charlie Kirk won't be able to spend Christmas with his family.

"Your honor, if you set it, it will happen," Neiman said. "Set it, please."

Graf set the next hearing for Monday, Nov. 9 at 1 p.m. MT, when he said he would read his ruling.

articles.title: Vanessa Trump 'finally cancer-free,' she says after health battle in emotional video with daughter Kai
articles.excerpt:
Vanessa Trump shares she's cancer-free after her breast cancer battle in a heartfelt conversation with daughter Kai and Dr. Nicole Saphier shared via Instagram.

Vanessa Trump revealed she is now canc...
articles.body_text:
Vanessa Trump shares she's cancer-free after her breast cancer battle in a heartfelt conversation with daughter Kai and Dr. Nicole Saphier shared via Instagram.

Vanessa Trump revealed she is now cancer-free after battling breast cancer, sharing the emotional health update in a new video with her daughter, Kai Trump, months after publicly announcing her diagnosis.

The 19-year-old granddaughter of President Donald Trump shared a preview of the conversation on Instagram during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, revealing that her mother, who's the ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr., was diagnosed in April.

"And my mom was diagnosed with breast cancer in April, so we thought we'd share her story and how she was diagnosed, how she overcame it," Kai said in the video.

KAI TRUMP REVEALS HOW FAMILY RALLIED AROUND MOM VANESSA AMID BREAST CANCER BATTLE: ‘IT’S A LONG JOURNEY’

Vanessa Trump, left, revealed she is now cancer-free after battling breast cancer, sharing the emotional health update in a new video with her daughter, Kai Trump. (TGL Golf via Getty Images, File)

To finish the social clip, Vanessa shared the news that she is now cancer-free.

"And it came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free," Vanessa said.

The video also features Fox News medical contributor Dr. Nicole Saphier, who discusses the importance of breast cancer awareness and early detection.

FORMER 'DWTS' HOST SAMANTHA HARRIS SURVIVED BREAST CANCER TWICE AFTER DOCTORS DISMISSED HER SYMPTOMS

Dr. Nicole Saphier shakes the hand of Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., ahead of her confirmation hearing to be surgeon general Sept. 16. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images, File)

"It feels different for everyone," Saphier said. "The reason I like social media talking about breast cancer is because it's reminding people that it is common."

In her Instagram caption, Kai said she sat down with her mother and Saphier to discuss Vanessa's cancer journey, prevention and early detection. She also announced that the full conversation would be released on YouTube the following day.

Vanessa, the mother of five, first revealed her breast cancer diagnosis in May.

"I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer," Vanessa wrote at the time. "While this isn't news anyone expects, I'm working closely with my medical team on a treatment plan."

She revealed that doctors had performed a procedure earlier that week and thanked her family for their support.

"I am staying focused and hopeful while surrounded by the love and support of my family, my kids, and those closest to me," she wrote.

KAI TRUMP OPENS UP ABOUT LEAVING HOME FOR COLLEGE, CREDITS PRESIDENT FOR GIVING HER 'COMPETITIVE EDGE'

Kai Trump opened up about the emotional experience with her mother in August. (James Gilbert/TGL/TGL Golf via Getty Images, File)

The announcement prompted support from Ivanka Trump, who wrote, "Praying for your continued strength and a swift recovery. Love you mama."

In June, Vanessa said she was recovering from surgery and preparing to begin the second stage of treatment, Fox News Digital reported.

Kai later opened up about the emotional experience in an August interview with Fox News Digital, shortly after beginning her freshman year at the University of Miami.

"There was definitely, there was a lot of crying in, like, the week leading up," Kai said of the days before leaving for college. "We would just be driving, and then we'd just start crying together."

At the time, Kai said her mother was improving after treatment.

"My mom, she's doing a lot better," she said. "Kind of after treatment, she wasn't feeling very good. Just like how treatment will make you feel … but she's getting a lot better now."

Vanessa Trump, left, first revealed her diagnosis and her daughter Kai described their emotional summer together. (Cliff Hawkins/Getty Images, File)

Kai described the extra time she spent with her mother over the summer as a "blessing in disguise."

"I was able to spend extra time with her that I would normally probably spend on the golf course," Kai said. "It was nice to spend those extra hours with her throughout the day before going to college."

Now, months after Vanessa first revealed her diagnosis and Kai described their emotional summer together, the mother and daughter are sharing a hopeful new chapter.

Fox News Digital's Sophia Compton and Paulina Dedaj contributed to this reporting.

Jasmine Baehr is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital, where she covers politics, the military, legal debates surrounding life and family policy, as well as faith and culture.

articles.title: Wrestling legend Ric Flair, 77, rushed to Tampa hospital after fall outside bar, head injuries: report
articles.excerpt: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel joins 'America's Newsroom' to break down Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary emboli. He also di...
articles.body_text:
Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel joins 'America's Newsroom' to break down Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary emboli. He also discusses rising e-bike injuries.

Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Florida hospital after falling outside a bar.

According to TMZ, Flair was at a Tampa bar when he walked outside and fell, injuring his face and possibly suffering a concussion.

TMZ says Flair cut his head and eye, which was bleeding, and was loaded into an ambulance.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Ric Flair attends the 44th Annual Sports Emmy Awards at Frederick P. Rose Hall, Jazz at Lincoln Center in New York City on May 22, 2023. (Arturo Holmes/Getty Images)

The reported fall came hours after Flair announced that he would be unable to attend a scheduled appearance in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg.

"My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First. Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening," Flair said on X. "We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice."

Flair said he is slated to have surgery on the affected vein, "[w]hich My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward."

"Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support," Flair added.

Tampa Fire Rescue told OutKick and Fox News Digital that it responded to a fall outside the establishment, and an adult male was taken to a local hospital — the department did not name Flair, saying they could not "provide any patient particulars due to HIPPA guidelines."

Flair, 77, has battled health and alcohol issues over the years.

FILE - Professional wrestler Ric Flair in attendance prior to the 2018 CFP national championship college football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Jan. 8, 2018. (Dale Zanine-USA TODAY Sports)

EX-WRESTLER PAC'S SUDDEN DEATH CAUSE REVEALED BY COOK COUNTY MEDICAL EXAMINER'S OFFICE

Flair has been in and out of wrestling for the last few years. His so-called "Last Match" took place in 2022 — a tag-team match with his then-son-in-law, the wrestler known as Andrade, against Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal. He later revealed he passed out twice during the match.

Flair made his All Elite Wrestling debut in 2023 and was a brief part of Sting’s final professional match at AEW Revolution, where Sting and Darby Allin took on the Young Bucks.

He was a World Championship Wrestling world heavyweight champion eight times, a National Wrestling Alliance world heavyweight champion nine times and a WWE champion twice during his career.

Ric Flair exclaims his trademark 'WOOO' at his Last Match press conference at the Fairgrounds in Nashville, Tenn., on June 23, 2022. (Abbey Cutrer / The Tennessean / USA TODAY NETWORK)

The WWE inducted Flair into its Hall of Fame in 2008 as a singles wrestler and as a member of the Four Horsemen in 2012.

articles.title: Rubio urges Cubans to work with CIA to bring political change to communist-run island
articles.excerpt: President Donald Trump teases that U.S. warships could stop near Cuba after Iran and send Secretary of State Marco Rubio in to "finish the job," during a midterm rally speech Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump teases that U.S. warships could stop near Cuba after Iran and send Secretary of State Marco Rubio in to "finish the job," during a midterm rally speech Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, in Fort Myers, Florida.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio urged Cubans seeking political change Friday to discreetly cooperate with the CIA as President Donald Trump separately floated sending Rubio to the communist-run island to negotiate a deal.

"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio wrote in a post on X.

"The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA."

RUBIO WARNS CUBA HAS INFILTRATED US WITH SPIES, CALLS COMMUNIST REGIME AN 'ESPIONAGE SUPERPOWER'

Rubio's message explicitly encouraged Cubans to work with the U.S. intelligence agency but did not identify a specific operation or explain what such cooperation would involve.

Rubio, the son of Cuban immigrants, has long advocated for a tougher U.S. approach toward the Cuban government.

The former Florida senator has been a prominent critic of the communist leadership in Havana and opposed efforts to normalize relations without political reforms.

Trump, meanwhile, raised the possibility of U.S. ships stopping near Cuba while discussing Iran during a midterm rally in Fort Myers, Florida, Friday.

TRUMP EXPANDS CUBA SANCTIONS BEYOND US COMPANIES IN MAJOR CRACKDOWN ON FOREIGN ENABLERS

Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks to reporters alongside White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, left, and CIA Director John Ratcliffe, center, after U.S. military actions in Venezuela at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Palm Beach, Fla., Jan. 3, 2026. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)

"Don't worry. We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran with it. We'll do a little stopover now. We'll do a little stopover," Trump told the crowd.

"Actually, what we're going to do with Cuba is we're going to come back from Iran. Those beautiful ships will pass Cuba. We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands."

Trump then suggested Rubio could handle negotiations with the communist-run island.

IRANIAN NEGOTIATORS KICKED OUT OF US AS TALKS STALL, TRUMP LAYS OUT 'POSSIBLE' TIMELINE FOR MORE STRIKES

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and US President Donald Trump speak to the press following US military actions in Venezuela, at Trump's Mar-a-Lago residence in Palm Beach, Fla., Jan. 3, 2026. (Jim Watson/AFP via Getty Images)

"And then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal. We'll have Marco. Marco. We don't even have to stop. We could just put him in there and he'll figure it out. He's a great guy."

Trump did not provide details about any proposed agreement with Cuba or indicate whether his remarks reflected an actual military or diplomatic plan.

Fox News Digital reached out to the CIA, State Department, White House and Cuban Embassy in Washington, D.C., for comment.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Trump says NFL 'could've probably postponed' Paris game as France protests stretch police thin
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump is skeptical about the National Football League continuing to hold its first-ever game in Paris amid protests.

The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are still set to k...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump is skeptical about the National Football League continuing to hold its first-ever game in Paris amid protests.

The Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are still set to kick off Sunday despite the civil unrest and a Paris Saint-Germain soccer game the same day being postponed.

Paris police requested a postponement of the PSG game because police and security resources are stretched thin due to mass protests, ongoing civil unrest and France's first NFL game happening in the region, per multiple reports.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

President Donald Trump speaks to members of the media on the South Lawn of the White House before boarding Marine One in Washington, D.C., on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

The NFL said in a reply to an email from OutKick and Fox News Digital that the PSG game did not impact any potential decision to move the Steelers-Saints game. However, Trump said the NFL "could've probably postponed that match."

"It's looking like tomorrow is going to be a bad day in France, so you worry about it. I would've said the NFL could've probably postponed that match... France is really in trouble," Trump told reporters on Friday.

Trump then took a shot at Democratic policies.

"That's what happens when you go left. That's what happens when you allow unlimited numbers of people into your country from very unfriendly countries."

The NFL has insisted multiple times this week that Sunday's game in France will be safe to play and safe for fans to attend amid civil unrest. However, the Steelers canceled a fan event in the area.

According to a league source, the topics discussed at the two-hour gathering included security for the game, the readiness of the Stade de France, where the game is to be played and the growth of flag football in France.

Organizers of the Paris protest told the Associated Press that an administrative court overturned a protest ban issued by police after they challenged it. The Paris prefecture previously said the ban was necessary, given the risk of street violence after groups of masked youth clashed with officers, looted shops and torched cars over the weekend.

The Steelers' travel plan ahead of their game at Paris' Stade de France against the New Orleans Saints is raising some eyebrows. (AP Photo/Greg Payan)

VANCE RECEIVES WARM RECEPTION DURING BENGALS VISIT DESPITE NEGATIVE MEDIA PORTRAYAL: SOURCE

The organizers signed a police document stating that the protest would remain stationary due to the risk of violence.

Earlier this week, Dani Watt, the wife of Steelers defensive end TJ Watt, questioned publicly why the game has not been moved.

"Tell me how this one makes sense???" Watt posted.

The NFL on Thursday told OutKick that its own NFL Fan House event scheduled for Friday and Saturday remains as scheduled.

"It's happening," a league spokesman said.

On Wednesday, NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he would attend the game and had spoken with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in recent days about moving forward with it.

A fire burns as police officers in riot gear stand guard during civil unrest in Paris, France, the day after a national day of demonstrations against the cost of living and rising fuel prices on Oct. 18, 2026. (Reuters)

Rubio told OutKick that the American embassy in France believes the game "will be fine."

OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

articles.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and flash flooding predicted for much of Australia
articles.excerpt:
Parts of Queensland, Victoria and South Australia can expect severe storms on Saturday, moving into NSW and Tasmania by Sunday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Severe thun...
articles.body_text:
Parts of Queensland, Victoria and South Australia can expect severe storms on Saturday, moving into NSW and Tasmania by Sunday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Severe thunderstorms and heavy rain will sweep across most Australian states this weekend, adding to the deluge in an already drenched Queensland.

Flash flooding in south-east Queensland this week prompted hundreds of SES callouts and the closure of multiple schools. On Saturday morning, the Bureau of Meteorology had nine flood warnings in place for south Queensland.

The BoM is now warning of severe thunderstorms, heavy rain and flash flooding across South Australia, Victoria, NSW, Tasmania.

Senior meteorologist at the Bureau of Meteorology, David Crock, said severe thunderstorms and heavy rain were forecast across multiple locations in central and eastern Queensland on Saturday, including Rockhampton, Gladstone, Bundaberg, the Sunshine Coast hinterlands and Roma.

Severe storms could also sweep through parts of Victoria, including Melbourne’s eastern suburbs and central and eastern South Australia. Heavy rain is expected to develop in Tasmania overnight into Sunday morning.

“There’s plenty of rain across the south-east, as well as plenty of showers and storms and rain across much of Queensland as well, after what’s already been a really wet week,” Crock said.

The cold front will move across NSW on Sunday, bringing severe thunderstorms to the west of the state as well as north-eastern Victoria, Sydney and Brisbane.

“Tomorrow is a threat for thunderstorms right across eastern Australia, with severe thunderstorms likely through a wide part of inland eastern Australia,” he said.

This week, multiple areas in Queensland were hit by more than twice their average October rainfall across a few days.

“It was an incredibly wet week in Queensland. Much more typical of summer or January or February than this time of year,” Crock said.

The Sunshine Coast hinterlands and Caboolture were hit by flash flooding and recorded a seven-day rainfall total of 300-400mm of rain, with some areas reaching 450mm.

“It’s been notable how persistent this weather pattern has been, how much moisture has pumped in … then how those rainfall totals have accumulated across seven to 10 days through Queensland and northern New South Wales,” Crock said.

On Thursday, torrential rain in south-east Queensland caused flash flooding, water rescues and hundreds of calls for help while several schools were forced to close on Friday.

Thursday’s heavy rain stretched from Caboolture down to the Border Ranges, with some places copping well over 200mm falls.

The Queensland fire department carried out more than 16 swift-water rescues, including using a raft to retrieve an elderly man clinging to the roof of his vehicle at Caboolture.

articles.title: Typhoon Champi hits Taiwan, killing one and injuring 350
articles.excerpt:
Typhoon Champi has struck Taiwan, killing one person and injuring at least 350 others, as authorities warned of “destructive winds” and instructed people to stay indoors.

The storm swept past the isl...
articles.body_text:
Typhoon Champi has struck Taiwan, killing one person and injuring at least 350 others, as authorities warned of “destructive winds” and instructed people to stay indoors.

The storm swept past the island’s northeast on Friday, toppling trees, shutting shops and schools, cutting power to thousands of households, and forcing more than 4,300 people to evacuate from their homes.

Champi is heading towards China and Japan, forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights in the region.

“From tonight through tomorrow morning conditions will be very windy and stormy everywhere,” Central Weather Administration (CWA) forecaster Lin Ping-yu said in a briefing. “Please try to stay indoors.”

Champi was briefly a super typhoon with winds of nearly 300 kilometres per hour (186 miles per hour) but has since weakened. The US Joint Typhoon Warning Center reported maximum winds of 185km/h (115mph).

Worse is still expected to come on Saturday. Champi could drop up to 900mm (35 inches) of rain between Thursday and Saturday, with the northeast hit hardest, the CWA said. More than 400mm fell in Yilan County on Friday.

CWA forecaster Lu Kuo-chen said the typhoon could slow near the island’s northeastern tip, prolonging its impact.

About 8,400 households in Japan’s Okinawa islands were without power on Friday afternoon, according to the Okinawa Electric Power Company. Champi is forecast to hover near Okinawa and then China’s eastern coast before turning northeast towards mainland Japan.

Champi is the latest storm in a Pacific season supercharged by El Nino.

The United Nations said on Wednesday that El Nino, a natural cycle that warms the tropical Pacific, is heading off the charts.

“The current El Nino event could be unprecedented in strength. Literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades,” said Celeste Saulo, secretary-general of the World Meteorological Organization.

It is expected to peak in December, with its impact lasting into 2027 and beyond.

articles.title: Father who killed Oregon school shooter speaks out for first time: ‘I have to go in’
articles.excerpt:
Kaylub Giamanco recounts the day he confronted the Silver Rail elementary school shooter, who killed three boys and one teacher

The Oregon father hailed as a hero for stopping a school shooting last ...
articles.body_text:
Kaylub Giamanco recounts the day he confronted the Silver Rail elementary school shooter, who killed three boys and one teacher

The Oregon father hailed as a hero for stopping a school shooting last week spoke for the first time about the incident, describing his experience and how he told a 911 operator: “I have to go in. People are going to die.”

Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old carpenter, has received national attention and praise for stopping the bloodshed at Silver Rail elementary in Bend, Oregon, where his children attend school.

He fatally shot Griffin J John II, a 16-year-old former student at the school, who broke in and shot six people, killing Megan Lambert, a 25-year-old teacher, and three children, including five-year-old Rhoam Summer.

In an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB), his first since the 15 October shooting, he recounted that day. He told reporters that he was only in the area because he had decided to return home and eat lunch with his wife rather than the meal he brought to work that day.

For a moment, Giamanco, who lives near the school, thought it was a prank when he saw a man in black armed with a gun headed toward Silver Rail, he said. Then he saw the man fire the gun and climb over a school fence. Giamanco pulled out a .40 caliber handgun from his center console and headed into the school parking lot, calling 911, before himself hopping over a fence to pursue the shooter.

He quietly followed Griffin without the teenager seeing him, at one point crawling on his hands and knees when he heard “children pleading for their lives”.

“I just started army crawling faster and faster and I told myself this is probably the last thing that I’m ever going to do,” he told OPB.

Giamanco crawled through a broken window and toward the special education class Griffin had entered, where a teacher was fighting with the shooter. He came into the classroom and fired his gun. Griffin fell and was reaching for his weapon before Giamanco, who said he “was afraid of him shooting anybody else”, shot him two more times.

He told OPB that he lies awake at night thinking of what he saw that day and the teenage perpetrator, and wonders if he could have done more.

“I want to apologize for not saving their babies,” Giamanco told the outlet. “The gratitude for saving people’s children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn’t save.”

Giamanco said he wants to see safer schools with school resource officers at every site, and that he would like to raise funding to support school safety efforts.

articles.title: ESPN posts propagandistic headline about Trump, LeBron and national anthem
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump calls out LeBron James and WNBA teams over their actions surrounding the national anthem during his Iowa rally.

NBA star LeBron James was shown practicing his golf swing during...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump calls out LeBron James and WNBA teams over their actions surrounding the national anthem during his Iowa rally.

NBA star LeBron James was shown practicing his golf swing during the playing of the United States national anthem before his 76ers debut on Tuesday. Later in the week, President Donald Trump called James' conduct a "TOTAL DISGRACE" on social media.

The story itself is quite simple. James practiced his golf swing during "The Star-Spangled Banner." Trump criticized him for it. And yet, the headline writers at ESPN apparently didn't see it quite as clearly.

According to ESPN.com on Thursday, "Trump criticizes LeBron James for not standing still during the national anthem."

Here's the full clip of James during the national anthem:

Describing what James did as merely "not standing still" is an awfully charitable characterization. He wasn't shifting his feet or adjusting his uniform. He was practicing his golf swing while the national anthem played.

The framing minimizes the conduct at the center of the controversy. ESPN suggested James' behavior was innocuous and Trump's criticism was excessive.

That was the point. ESPN must feel it has an obligation to protect James. The headline writers must have also agreed James was wrong. Otherwise, there would be no reason to sanitize it as James merely failing to "stand still."

At least athletes who kneel during the anthem generally claim that they are doing so as a form of protest. James offered no such explanation. He simply sought to make a mockery of the anthem.

President Donald Trump's 2022 remarks about recruiting LeBron James to a women's basketball team went viral in August 2026. (Getty Images)

It also wasn't the first time. James was caught practicing his swing during the national anthem on Christmas Day last year.

There’s something cringe about a star American athlete who previously criticized NBA executive Daryl Morey for supporting Hong Kong protesters now behaving this way during the U.S. national anthem.

Los Angeles Lakers forward LeBron James (23) speaks to a reporter after the game against the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center. (Stephen Lew/Imagn Images)

At this stage of his career, the NBA also has to ask how much James still benefits its brand.

James turns 42 in December. He has averaged 15 points per game through his first two games this season and, unsurprisingly at his age, is a shell of his former self.

His basketball legacy is secure. James is one of the greatest players in NBA history. But he has become a net negative through his declining play and consistently anti-American messaging.

articles.title: Blue Planet III features cloudier footage to prove authenticity amid AI boom
articles.excerpt:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say

The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, ...
articles.body_text:
BBC series deliberately uses ‘more organic’ shots to assure viewers animals are not AI-generated, producers say

The David Attenborough-narrated series Blue Planet III deliberately includes cloudier, less polished footage to counter AI fakery and assure viewers it is “authentic”, its producers have said.

Nearly a decade after Blue Planet II shone a light on plastic pollution, and 25 years since the first Blue Planet aired, the hit BBC series is returning with more animal behaviour and cutting-edge technology, including the world’s first underwater CCTV camera – dubbed “stonefish” cam.

Since the first Blue Planet, TVs and cameras have evolved to give viewers sharper, higher definition pictures. But the combination of the rise in AI and the extraordinary sequences and fantastical creatures captured by BBC Studios’ natural history unit for this series led producers to include what they called more “organic” footage and less polished shots, to show that the animals were not AI-generated.

The executive producer, Elizabeth White, said AI, “makes us want to be even more authentic”, adding that the creatures filmed in the deep ocean “are probably more remarkable than AI could imagine and it’s completely real”.

She said that in the past “the amount of plankton and things that are in the water in the sequences” would usually mean they might be excluded, and previously, “we might have framed out a boat or a buoy or gone: ‘Oh, actually … the water conditions are not really good enough for this.’”

But now such things are being left in as “we’re really leaning into that authenticity … As AI booms we will probably lean more into the more organic”, murkier and less polished footage.

For the first time, the BBC’s specialist factual commissioning head, Jack Bootle, assured journalists at a press screening: “No gen AI was used in this series. Not a single frame. It’s all real photography.”

Bootle added that as we live in a “golden age of natural history-making … sometimes people feel like they’ve seen it all before [so] this series is bursting with novel behaviour”.

That includes never-before-seen action of dolphins using sea sponges to block holes in coral to trap fish, captured using underwater CCTV – developed by the programme’s producer and director, Yoland Bosiger.

Over the four years of filming across five oceans, BBC Studios “continually innovated”, said the series producer, Lara Bickerton, creating a “mini-dome” camera to follow an octopus, a “deep-sea selfie stick”, camera operators wearing leg-mounted scooters to create immersive TikTok-style diving footage and using lasers to film deep-sea creatures.

Other remarkable animal behaviour captured in the programme includes grouper communicating with another species of fish; 200,000 crabs lining up in formation to feed; sea urchins using shells as sun hats; and footage involving penguins that echoes the Planet Earth II, ‘iguana v snakes’ sequence.

Threats to the ocean as well as its resilience are addressed in the series. Episodes show how the climatecrisis is killing off the sea where anemone clown fish live and what they do to try to fix their homes, and the issue of plastics raised in Blue Planet II continues with a story about pollutants [and] forever chemicals, said White.

Bosiger said Attenborough, who is 100 years old, was “very much involved” and made changes to scripts.

White added: “What’s wonderful is he hasn’t lost his curiosity … he’s still that little boy … who gets excited … when you show him a new piece of footage.”

Asked if the BBC’s £500m cost-cutting drive would affect BBC Studios’ renowned natural history reputation, White said she could not comment on that but pointed out that Blue Planet III made savings by using more local crews on location than in previous series.

Blue Planet III starts Sunday 1 November on BBC1 and iPlayer

articles.title: Vance receives warm reception during Bengals visit despite negative media portrayal: source
articles.excerpt:
Vice President JD Vance is greeted by Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor outside of the team's locker room while visiting a recent practice.

The narrative on social media that Vice President JD...
articles.body_text:
Vice President JD Vance is greeted by Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor outside of the team's locker room while visiting a recent practice.

The narrative on social media that Vice President JD Vance was ignored by multiple Cincinnati Bengals players at a recent team practice apparently does not reflect what actually unfolded that day, a source with knowledge of the visit told OutKick.

A recent video shared online showed Vance and his family outside the team's locker room on Thursday as the team walked back in. The video, that did not have clear audio of the interaction, showed Bengals tight end Drew Sample stop to shake the vice president's hand as other players walked by.

But footage obtained by OutKick portrayed a different story, including a handshake with an enthusiastic Bengals head coach Zac Taylor. The video also captured audio and appeared to show Vance chopping it up with players and other staffers.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Vice President JD Vance visits the Cincinnati Bengals' practice facility. (OutKick)

"Seeing how the media works is actually pretty crazy. The players, staff, and Vice President Vance and his son all had a great time at practice," the source told OutKick exclusively. "All of these negative tweets and articles are completely detached from the reality of how well the visit went."

Initial reaction to the video shared on social described the interaction as Vance getting "snubbed" by the team.

"This is what TOTAL HUMILIATION looks like: JD Vance attempted to greet Cincinnati Bengals players in the locker room and got snubbed and ghosted by every single player except one," one person wrote on X.

"JD Vance walked into the Bengals locker room looking for a photo-op, and the players gave him the cold shoulder he deserves," another person wrote, adding that the team didn't want to be used for"political theater."

But the source told OutKick that Vance and his son were warmly received when visiting the facility with no planned media engagement. A photo obtained by OutKick showed the vice president and his family playing catch on the field. The source added that defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence approached the vice president and had conversation with him during the visit.

JD Vance and Dexter Lawrence chat at Cincinnati Bengals practice. (X/@VPRapidDirector)

TITANS PLAYER WHO GOT INTO ARGUMENT THAT PROVOKED 'UNFORTUNATE' GUN INCIDENT SPEAKS OUT

Vance, an Ohio native, is a longtime Bengals fan, growing up roughly an hour outside of Cincinnati. He has a home in Cincinnati’s East Walnut Hills neighborhood.

Vance toured the team's locker room, shook hands with several players, coach Zac Taylor and others, and came away with a football. It is unclear if Vance brought the ball to be autographed or the club gave it to him as a memento.

Quarterback Joe Burrow said he "did not" talk to Vance.

"He came with everybody and left with swiftness and efficiency before the end of practice, so I didn't get to," Burrow told reporters earlier this week.

JD Vance chats with members of the Cincinnati Bengals at practice. (X/@VPRapidDirector)

Vance was in town to deliver a speech at the FBI's Cincinnati Field Office and then hold a campaign rally at the Sharonville Convention Center.

OutKick's Armando Salguero contributed to this report.

articles.title: MSG uses Knicks championship rings as bait in phishing test, calls the lure 'an unfortunate mistake'
articles.excerpt: After a 53-year wait, the New York Knicks captured their first NBA championship, sparking celebrations across New York City. Thousands of fans lined the streets of Manhattan for a historic ticker-tape...
articles.body_text:
After a 53-year wait, the New York Knicks captured their first NBA championship, sparking celebrations across New York City. Thousands of fans lined the streets of Manhattan for a historic ticker-tape parade, turning a Thursday workday into a spontaneous holiday as the city honored its victorious team.

The New York Knicks found themselves in hot water late Thursday when it was reported that the organization did not give championship rings to its assistant coaches or other employees.

But the news took a turn when employees reportedly were given a phishing test email disguised as a chance to redeem their rings.

"Those who did click the link at the bottom of the message did not get to choose any jewelry; instead, they were forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class to help satisfy some of [owner James] Dolan’s growing cybersecurity concerns," The Athletic reported.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks reacts after receiving his championship ring during the Ring Ceremony and Banner Raising at Madison Square Garden on Oct. 20, 2026. (Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The team confirmed on Friday that the email was indeed a cybersecurity test.

"The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers. MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack," MSG said in a statement.

The company added that "[u]sing the rings as a lure to gain employees' attention was an unfortunate mistake" and said it would be giving "more than 275 championship rings and jewelry to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family, worth more than $3.7 million, in recognition of their contributions and celebrating this achievement."

New York Knicks owner James Dolan speaks during a championship celebration and Key to the City ceremony at City Hall Plaza after a ticker-tape parade honoring the team's NBA Finals victory in New York City on June 18, 2026. (Angela Weiss/AFP)

KNICKS SUPERFANS NAME THEIR NEWBORN 'KNICKSON FYVE' TO HONOR HISTORIC NBA CHAMPIONSHIP RUN

The Knicks hung their championship banner, their first since 1973, on Tuesday night in their season opener, and players received extravagant 22-carat rings that are estimated to be worth at least $100,000 each. Each ring has roughly 800 diamonds and a recreation of the world's most famous arena.

Coaches were reportedly told they would eventually receive rings but did not get them along with the players on Tuesday. Employees, however, were apparently told not to expect any.

That's when employees' hopes were raised when they got the phishing email about rings last month.

The New York Knicks look toward their new banner after receiving championship rings during a ring ceremony and banner raising to celebrate the team's NBA Championship win before a game against the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden on Oct. 20, 2026, in New York City. (Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

"(Employee name), this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you. There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below," the email reportedly said.

The Knicks beat the San Antonio Spurs in five games over the summer.

articles.title: Macron condemns racism after one killed in ‘terrorist’ shooting near Paris
articles.excerpt:
Gunman opens fire from car in Trappes and Verrière, killing one and injuring five others, including a 12-year-old girl

Emmanuel Macron has condemned racism in French society after a gunman opened fir...
articles.body_text:
Gunman opens fire from car in Trappes and Verrière, killing one and injuring five others, including a 12-year-old girl

Emmanuel Macron has condemned racism in French society after a gunman opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person, wounding a 12-year-old girl and injuring four others in what the president called a “racist terrorist attack”.

Macron arrived at the scene of the drive-by shooting in Trappes on Friday night, saying he was deeply saddened by what he called the “premeditated” attack. The 12-year-old girl, who was shot eight times, is being treated in hospital.

“What happened today ​marks a turning point for our ⁠country; what happened today ​was ​a terrorist ​and racist attack,” ​Macron said.

He said the gunman had targeted people because of the colour of their skin. The president said racism had often become part of the “ambient discourse in France” and created “an atmosphere”.

He said: “Don’t let this terrorist attack divide us.” He called for “respect and unity”, saying many French people would be scared and thinking “this could happen to me”.

Ali Rabeh, the leftwing mayor of Trappes, said the gunman had set out by car on Friday morning “firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath” as he drove through the town and neighbouring La Verrière. The mayor called it “objectively a racist attack, probably Islamophobic”.

Rabeh, whose family has Moroccan roots, said: “The people targeted today could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law.

“A 12-year-old girl is between life and death after being targeted by a volley of automatic gunfire in our country. Her crime was probably being of colour,” he added. “It’s probably one of the first attempts at a mass crime of Islamophobia and racism.”

Rabeh said everyone in France had a responsibility to bring “calm and harmony”. He called for a collective condemnation of rhetoric that “ideologically arms those capable of carrying out such acts”.

Anti-terrorism prosecutors are investigating whether the gunman targeted the “real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion” of the victims.

The 39-year-old suspect, who was stopped by police in his car, was named by France’s anti-terrorism prosecutor as Kevin T. He had driven through the towns of Trappes and La Verrière in Yvelines at about 10.30am on Friday. Over the course of 15 minutes, he repeatedly fired an automatic weapon, first at a petrol station, then a medical centre and a children’s playground.

The French public broadcaster reported that he shot dead a young black man, then targeted a woman wearing a headscarf, before shooting the 12-year-old girl, who was being treated for her eight gunshot wounds at a children’s hospital on Friday night.

The prosecutor said in a statement on Friday night that the medical status of the five wounded victims was not stable.

The man killed was named as Pengo Bossio Wangi in an Instagram post by the mixed martial arts academy of which he was a member. The Atch Academy paid tribute to a man who “set an example” and said that memories of “his smile, his energy, and his generosity will remain etched within our walls and in our hearts”.

Nicolas Dainville, the mayor of La Verrière, told Agence France-Presse that two of the wounded people in his town were cleaners of African origin attending to a school Friday on morning when the shooter got out of his car to open fire.

The prosecutor said that when the suspect was stopped by police in his car he was found with a sten gun – a British submachine gun used in the second world war – as well as teargas grenades.

The man had also booby-trapped his home with gas canisters and electric wires connected to a timer, authorities said, adding that a member of his family was arrested and taken into custody for questioning.

“The investigations are ongoing, but it is clearly a terrorist crime. It is an extremely serious act,” the interior minister, Laurent Nunez, told reporters from ⁠Yvelines.

The ‌shooting comes at a moment of particular tension in France. Last Saturday saw one of the most violent days of unrest in years, which left public buildings burned, hundreds of shops destroyed and looted, and at least 2,400 people arrested in cities across the country.

Renewed protests, over teacher shortages and crumbling buildings in high schools as well as the high cost of living, are expected on Saturday.

Marine Le Pen, the leader of the far-right anti-immigration the National Rally party, is polling highly ahead of next spring’s presidential election when Macron steps down.

After the Trappes attack, Fabien Roussel, a Communist candidate, wrote on social media that the far right was responsible for “racist hatred” in France.

Le Pen condemned what she called the “abject motive of racism” of the “barbaric act”.

Additional reporting by Yassin El-Moudden

articles.title: Craig Carton explains why the NFL has some questions to ask after bizarre moment in Bears-Patriots game
articles.excerpt:
Craig Carton has some questions for Malik Muhammed after a play caught his attention during the Chicago Bears Thursday Night Football showdown against the New England Patriots.

Sports betting is a bi...
articles.body_text:
Craig Carton has some questions for Malik Muhammed after a play caught his attention during the Chicago Bears Thursday Night Football showdown against the New England Patriots.

Sports betting is a big part of the sports experience these days, and unfortunately, that will lead to questions about the game's integrity, as OutKick's Craig Carton pointed out on Friday's edition of "The Craig Carton Show."

The Chicago Bears took on the New England Patriots on Thursday, and there was a certain play late in the first half that caught Carton's attention.

Patriots running back Rhamondre Stephenson caught a screen pass at midfield and somehow took it all the way to the house for a late touchdown with no time left on the clock. But it was what Bears DB Malik Muhammad did on the play that had Carton asking questions.

RHAMONDRE STEVENSON'S MIRACULOUS 48-YARD TOUCHDOWN STUNS BEARS AS CLOCK EXPIRES IN FIRST HALF

Did... did Muhammad turn and run in the complete opposite direction that Stephenson was headed?

Well, it's at least worth asking some questions.

NBA AND MANY SPORTSBOOKS AGREE TO BAN MULTIPLE TYPES OF BETS DUE TO RECENT BETTING SCANDALS

OutKick's Craig Carton had some questions after a strange play by Chicago Bears defensive back Malik Muhammad on Thursday night against the New England Patriots. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh))

"What Malik Muhammad does next is why every single person that is against legalized wagering thinks the fix is in," he said. "Rather than step into the hole and make an attempt to tackle Stevenson, he literally runs away from the play."

Whether it was a bad read or something else, there's really no question: that was about as big a whiff as you'll see in the NFL.

Fortunately, that play didn't have any impact on the game as the Bears won and covered the spread.

Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson watches from the sideline during the first half of an NFL football game against the Minnesota Vikings in Chicago, Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (AP Photo/Nam Y. Huh)

Carton noted that the play likely got more attention because it was on a Thursday night, and that the NFL should be asking some questions.

"And that's the type of play that needs to be investigated," he said. "The NFL now has to sit down and interview Malik Muhammad and interview Ben Johnson of the Bears and get an explanation as to why (Muhammad was) running away from the ball carrier? Like it makes no sense at all. There's not even a logical, reasonable explanation of 'Well, I was going this way because I thought he might cut outside.'

"No, there was no chance to cut outside because by you coming this way, you opened up a seven-yard gap."
